name: genesis-browser
content:
.TH GENESIS-BROWSER 7 "November 2026" "Genesis 0.2.0" "Genesis Manual"
.SH NAME
genesis-browser \- Genesis's internet browser: Chrome over CDP
.SH SYNOPSIS
.nf
\fBparietal_lobe.arc_web._Browser\fR   the transport itself
\fBweb_search\fR                      the tool that browses with it
.fi
.SH DESCRIPTION
Genesis's web browser is Google Chrome, launched per host by
\fI_browser_binary()\fR — \fBgoogle-chrome\fR first, then
\fBgoogle-chrome-stable\fR, \fBchromium\fR, \fBchromium-browser\fR;
\fBGENESIS_BROWSER\fR pins an override. She does not drive it with
pixels and hope: every act and percept crosses the Chrome DevTools
Protocol on a websocket — \fBPage.navigate\fR to travel,
\fBInput.dispatchKeyEvent\fR and \fBInput.dispatchMouseEvent\fR for
real key and mouse events, \fBRuntime.evaluate\fR to read the DOM,
and \fBNetwork.getResponseBody\fR to pull the bodies the page
itself fetched.
.PP
Two modes: \fBheadless\fR (the default — scoring runs and
background fetches need no window) and \fBheaded\fR, which opens on
her own nested display — the Xephyr screen
\fIensure_arc_display()\fR keeps for her — never on the user's
desktop.
.SH PROFILE — HER MEMORY OF THE WEB
The browser's user-data dir is persistent: it is
\fI<data_dir>/browser/<purpose>\fR, not a tempdir. Cookies, site
state, and history survive restarts — a browser that forgets every
session is not one she learns from. There are two purposes:
.TP
.B web
The browsing her tools do — search and fetch through
\fIfrontal_lobe.tools.web_search\fR.
.PP
The separation is a Chrome requirement: two instances cannot share
one user-data dir — a second launch forwards to the first and
exits. The dirs are also never the host's default Chrome profile,
which is what keeps \fB--remote-debugging-port\fR honoured: Chrome
\(>=136 silently ignores remote debugging on the default data
directory.
.SH LAUNCH
She invokes it as:
.PP
.nf
\fBgoogle-chrome\fR [\fB--headless=new\fR]
    \fB--remote-debugging-port=0\fR
    \fB--no-first-run --no-default-browser-check\fR
    \fB--disable-gpu --mute-audio\fR
    \fB--disable-dev-shm-usage\fR
    \fB--password-store=basic --use-mock-keychain\fR
    \fB--disable-sync\fR
    \fB--window-size=\fR\fIW,H\fR
    \fB--user-data-dir=\fR\fI<data_dir>/browser/<purpose>\fR
.fi
.PP
Port 0 lets the browser pick a free port and write it to
\fIDevToolsActivePort\fR in the profile dir — a fixed port makes
two runs collide. The keyring is mocked because a persistent
profile would else block on an unlock prompt no one can answer.
\fB--disable-sync\fR keeps her profile from replicating outward to
a Google account; site logins within it still work.
.SH ENVIRONMENT
.TP
.B GENESIS_BROWSER
Pin the browser executable — a name on \fBPATH\fR or an absolute
path.
.TP
.B GENESIS_DATA_DIR
The root her browser profiles live under (default
\fI~/.local/share/genesis\fR).
.TP
.B DISPLAY
Only in headed mode: her nested screen, never the user's.
.SH FILES
.TP
.I <data_dir>/browser/web
Her everyday browsing profile — persists.
.TP
.I DevToolsActivePort
Written by Chrome into the profile dir each launch; the port it
actually bound.
.TP
.I google-chrome(1) / google-chrome-stable(1)
The system's manual for the browser binary itself.
.SH SEE ALSO
.BR genesis (1),
.BR genesis-cli (1),
.BR genesis-math (7),
.BR google-chrome (1)
